tasks.title: Analyze current ownership and identify thick owners
tasks.description: Run graphify and module-doc checks to identify high-connection files and current ownership boundaries. Document the current state of thick owners (OpenCodianView.ts, OpenCodeService.ts, main.ts, ServerManager.ts) and their responsibility density.
tasks.details: Execute `npm run check:graphify` and `npm run check:module-docs` to generate reports. Review `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` and existing `docs/modules/**` files. For each thick owner, list its current responsibilities, import surface, and adjacent owners. This analysis will inform task selection and ensure each subsequent task improves ownership shape.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the analysis produces a clear mapping of thick files to their responsibilities and adjacent owners. No code changes are made; validation is manual review of generated reports.

tasks.title: Thin ServerManager.ts by moving a complete behavior slice to an adjacent owner
tasks.description: Identify a complete local-server lifecycle or endpoint-resolution slice in ServerManager.ts that can be moved into an existing adjacent owner (e.g., a config or storage owner) without changing behavior. Perform the extraction, update module docs, and run verification.
tasks.details: Primary owner type: domain runtime owner. Analyze ServerManager.ts for a slice that is self-contained (e.g., server configuration loading or endpoint resolution). Move that slice into an existing adjacent owner (e.g., a config owner in `src/core/config/` or storage owner in `src/core/storage/`). Ensure the new location is a durable owner (not a thin wrapper). Update `docs/modules/` files to reflect the boundary change. Do not create new one-off files. Run `npm run verify`, `npm run check:module-docs`, and `npm run check:graphify`.
tasks.testStrategy: Write focused Jest tests for the moved slice in its new owner. Verify that existing tests still pass. Run `npm run verify` and confirm no regression. Check that module docs are updated and graphify report shows improved ownership.

tasks.title: Thin OpenCodeService.ts by moving facade-adjacent logic into existing opencode owners
tasks.description: Move compatibility/facade-adjacent logic from OpenCodeService.ts into existing opencode owners such as lifecycle, prompt, session-control, query, state, or streaming coordinators. Do not add new runtime ownership to OpenCodeService.ts.
tasks.details: Primary owner type: high-connection facade owner. Review OpenCodeService.ts for methods that delegate to other services or coordinate between subsystems. Move those delegations into the appropriate existing owners (e.g., move prompt-related logic to a prompt owner, session control to a session owner). Ensure OpenCodeService.ts remains as a thin facade that only composes lifecycle. Update module docs. Run verification.
tasks.testStrategy: Ensure that after extraction, OpenCodeService.ts has fewer responsibilities. Run existing tests and add focused tests for the moved logic in their new owners. Run `npm run verify` and `npm run check:module-docs`.

tasks.title: Thin OpenCodianView.ts by extending existing chat services/coordinators
tasks.description: Reduce shell assembly or callback-surface density in OpenCodianView.ts by moving behavior into existing chat services or coordinators. Do not create one-off helpers. Do not add new runtime ownership to OpenCodianView.ts.
tasks.details: Primary owner type: high-connection facade owner. Identify callback handlers or UI assembly logic in OpenCodianView.ts that can be moved into existing chat services (e.g., message handling, view state management). Extend those services to own the behavior. Keep OpenCodianView.ts as a thin shell that wires UI components. Update module docs. Run verification.
tasks.testStrategy: Write tests for the moved behavior in the target services. Ensure OpenCodianView.ts tests still pass. Run `npm run verify` and `npm run check:module-docs`.

tasks.title: Thin main.ts by moving config/bootstrap slices into existing owners
tasks.description: Move complete config/bootstrap slices from main.ts into existing config, storage, or theme owners. Preserve plugin lifecycle ownership in main.ts.
tasks.details: Primary owner type: lifecycle composition owner. Identify initialization logic in main.ts that belongs to config (e.g., plugin settings loading), storage (e.g., data directory setup), or theme (e.g., applying theme). Move those slices into the respective owners. Ensure main.ts retains only lifecycle orchestration (onload, onunload, etc.). Update module docs. Run verification.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that main.ts is thinner and that moved logic works in its new owner. Run existing tests and add focused tests for the moved slices. Run `npm run verify` and `npm run check:module-docs`.

tasks.title: Update module documentation and verify ownership improvements
tasks.description: Update all affected `docs/modules/**` files to reflect boundary changes from tasks 10-13. Run full verification suite and confirm that ownership shape has improved or been explicitly preserved.
tasks.details: For each module boundary change, update the corresponding markdown file in `docs/modules/` to describe the new ownership. Ensure that the documentation clearly states the primary owner type and responsibilities. Run `npm run verify`, `npm run check:module-docs`, `npm run check:graphify`, and `npm run check:devlog-order`. Confirm that no thick files have grown and that ownership is clearer.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the full verification suite. Check that `npm run check:module-docs` passes and that graphify report shows reduced connection density for the thinned files. Manual review of documentation accuracy.
